At 27.8B dense parameters it is sized to run on a single GPU while accepting text, images and video, with a 262K native context extensible to roughly 1M tokens via YaRN and an adjustable reasoning_effort control. Alibaba's own card reports 61.7 on SWE-bench Pro and 90.3 on LiveCodeBench v6 - above the Claude Opus 4.6 Max figures it cites (53.4 and 88.8) - plus 73.0 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 89.2 GPQA Diamond against Meta Muse Glimmer 30B's 51.7 and 83.5. Every launch number is vendor-reported and several benchmarks (QwenSWEBench, CoWorkBench) are in-house, so independent confirmation is still outstanding.

models.name: GLM-5.3-Flash
models.params: 320B total / 18B active (MoE) - hybrid attention mixing KDA linear-attention layers with NoPE sparse MLA layers
models.modality: natively multimodal (text + image + video in), text out
models.pricing: $0.15 in / $0.03 cached in / $0.50 out per 1M (50% launch discount via ZAI through Sep 9 2026)
models.notable: The first GLM-5 model Z.ai describes as natively multimodal, and the cheapest model yet to reach an Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index of 57 - a point above Claude Opus 4.8 and level-plus with Gemini 3.7 Flash, at roughly nine cents per Index task. It spent its first week running anonymously as 'Ox Alpha' on OpenCode and OpenRouter, served entirely on domestically produced Chinese AI chips, before Z.ai revealed the identity on Aug 26. Three architecture changes carry the efficiency: hybrid KDA linear-attention plus NoPE sparse MLA layers, an IndexPool compression scheme Z.ai credits with a 4.4x smaller KV cache, and Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections. Weights ship under MIT on Hugging Face, and the model gives 3x the usable quota of full GLM-5.3 across every GLM Coding Plan tier.

models.name: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
models.params: 125B backbone + 51B N-gram embedding table + 4B multi-token-prediction module (~180B on disk) / 6B active per token
models.notable: Not a flagship - Alibaba shipped it explicitly as an early preview of the architecture that will underpin Qwen4, open-sourcing weights and an FP8 build at 11pm Beijing time on Aug 26. Four changes debut here: hybrid attention mixing Gated DeltaNet across 75% of layers with Qwen Sparse Attention on the rest, a Gated Residual with four parallel branches, a 20-million-entry N-gram lookup table that adds deterministic capacity without adding active compute, and Muon paired with AdamW during training. Alibaba says it trained for roughly one-ninth the cost of Qwen3.7-Plus. Every benchmark above is vendor-reported and not yet independently reproduced. Licensed qwen-community-1.0, and at 172.78 GiB in FP8 it needs multi-GPU serving rather than a workstation.

models.name: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp
models.params: 284B total / 13B active (MoE, same foundation as DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731)
models.pricing: $0.22 in / $0.007 cached in / $0.66 out per 1M (images billed at text-token rates, max 384 tokens per image)
models.notable: An experimental vision build of the cheap V4-Flash line, adding native image input while DeepSeek says it matches V4-Flash exactly on text - agents, reasoning and world knowledge. The point is agent workflows that never leave the model: screenshots, charts and document images go in under the same token pricing, via base64, external URL, or the free Files API, which lets one uploaded image be reused across requests without re-upload. DeepSeek claims a major jump over V4-Flash on multimodal agent benchmarks, putting multimodal agent performance close to Claude Opus 4.8, but published the comparison as a chart without numbers. No model card, license, or weights have accompanied the experimental vision build.

models.name: Gemini 3.5 Transcribe
models.modality: audio in, formatted text out (speech-to-text; streaming and non-streaming endpoints)
models.notable: Google's speech-to-text model, unveiled at I/O in May and fully launched with a model card on Aug 26 2026. Artificial Analysis measures a 2.6% word error rate non-streaming and 4.0% streaming, and Google claims a 70% improvement in transcription time over 2025's Chirp 3. It does more than transcribe: it strips filler words, resolves the speaker's own self-corrections, auto-formats the output, honors custom vocabulary and jargon, auto-detects more than 85 languages, and diarizes up to three speakers with timestamps on pre-recorded audio. Shipping now in Gboard Rambler on Android, the Gemini macOS app and Google Antigravity, with Chrome to follow; developers get it in public preview through the Gemini API and AI Studio, enterprises through the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform.

models.name: Thomson
models.params: not disclosed (specialized from an open-source base)
models.notable: Thomson Reuters' first proprietary LLM, built by specializing a strong open-source base on the company's own legal, tax and news archive - less than 10% of its total content used so far. Roughly $40M spent on training and compute, which the company frames as a fraction of a comparable frontier run. The commercial version is closed and ships first inside CoCounsel Legal as a Tabular Analysis document-review feature; a small open-weight version is on Hugging Face for academic and non-commercial use. Thomson Reuters claims parity with 'the latest frontier models across a range of tasks' but published no benchmark scores, and no independent evaluation exists yet. Notable mainly as a vertical, fully-owned alternative to renting a general frontier model.

models.name: Wan 3.0
models.context: not applicable (video model); accepts up to 10 images, 5 videos, 5 audio clips, documents up to 100MB, or one public webpage
models.modality: text + image + video + audio + document/webpage in, video with synchronized audio out
models.pricing: $0.05 per second at 480p to $0.20 per second at 1080p - a full 30-second 1080p clip runs about $6
models.notable: Alibaba's Tongyi Lab video model, in public beta from Aug 6 2026 and formally released Aug 24, a day after the company's $10B share sale. It generates clips of up to 30 seconds at 480p, 720p or 1080p - double the 15-second ceiling of Wan 2.7 - with audio generation on by default, multilingual voice output and synchronized micro-expressions. Its distinguishing feature is document-to-video: generation can be grounded directly in a structured source - a PDF, Word file, PowerPoint deck or public webpage - rather than requiring the user to convert that source into a text prompt first. It also adds intelligent duration recommendation and multi-round video extension. Access runs through Alibaba Cloud's Model Studio API (in preview) and Chinese consumer surfaces including the Qwen app and Qwen Creation. Unlike Wan 2.2, no weights had appeared on Wan's GitHub or Hugging Face as of Aug 25, making this a closed release; independent testing by Atlas Cloud reported repeated unwanted cuts mid-shot despite better visual fidelity and character consistency than Wan 2.7.

models.name: IBM Granite 4.2 30B
models.notable: The largest of IBM's Granite 4.2 family, released Aug 25 2026 under Apache 2.0 and IBM's first Granite generation with native reasoning. It is a plain decoder-only transformer - grouped-query attention with 8 KV heads, RoPE at theta 10,000,000, SwiGLU MLPs, RMSNorm - not a mixture-of-experts or hybrid-Mamba design, pre-trained from scratch on roughly 15 trillion tokens including about 1 trillion synthetic code tokens. Every size gets a switchable thinking mode; the 8B and 30B additionally go through agentic reinforcement learning inside real sandboxed environments, learning to edit code, drive a terminal and run web searches through harnesses such as OpenHands and SWE-agent. A speculative-decoding layer ships with the model, and FP8 and NVFP4 quantizations are supported under vLLM. Artificial Analysis scored it at 24 on the Intelligence Index on Aug 26 - far below the frontier, and positioned squarely as an enterprise model you can run yourself rather than a leaderboard contender.

models.name: IBM Granite 4.2 8B
models.notable: The mid-size Granite 4.2 model, Apache 2.0 and the smallest of the family to receive agentic reinforcement-learning post-training alongside the 30B. Same decoder-only recipe as its larger sibling - grouped-query attention, RoPE, SwiGLU, RMSNorm, roughly 15 trillion pre-training tokens - with a switchable thinking mode and speculative decoding for cheaper inference. It scores 47.67 on SWE-bench Verified, within ten points of the 30B, which is the point of the release: IBM is aiming at enterprises that want a self-hosted agent model small enough to serve cheaply rather than a frontier score. Artificial Analysis rates it 20 on the Intelligence Index. Weights ship on Hugging Face with vLLM, FP8 and NVFP4 support; a 3B variant covers Ollama and LM Studio on local hardware.

models.name: Tencent Hy4 preview
models.params: 770B total, 49B active (mixture-of-experts; 78 layers, 256 routed experts + 1 shared, top-8 routing)
models.notable: Tencent Hunyuan's next-generation flagship, released and open-sourced the same day under Apache 2.0 - a 770B-parameter mixture-of-experts model that activates 49B per token and carries a 1M-token context. It uses gated DeepSeek-style sparse attention with an IndexCache, and Tencent ships both BF16 and FP8 weights on Hugging Face. The pitch is practical engineering rather than a frontier score: it posts 85.4 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 82.9 on SWE-bench Multilingual, ahead of GLM-5.3 (81.3), Kimi K3 (80.8) and DeepSeek-V4-Pro (77.3), and jumps from 28.0 to 64.3 on DeepSWE against its predecessor. On SWE-bench Pro it reaches 65.7, above GLM-5.3 and Kimi K3 but well behind Claude Opus 5 at 79.2. Tencent says an internal panel of 163 experts scoring 203 engineering tasks rated it 2.99 of 4, above GLM-5.3 (2.92) and Kimi K3 (2.94), and that the model raised its own systems' throughput 31.8%. API access runs through Tencent Cloud TokenHub and OpenRouter at $0.834 in / $2.501 out per million tokens, with two weeks of free access via WorkBuddy and CodeBuddy.

models.name: Cohere Parse 5
models.context: per-page document input (PDF, PPT or JPEG as base64 data URI)
models.notable: A narrow 2.3B-parameter vision-language model, parse-v5.0, that converts enterprise documents into clean Markdown for downstream AI pipelines. It returns text in reading order, tables rendered as HTML, lists, form key-value pairs, image descriptions and bounding-box coordinates for visual elements. Cohere positioned it explicitly on price-to-performance rather than raw accuracy - it does not top document-understanding leaderboards, but at $1.50 per 1,000 pages it is aimed at organizations parsing millions of pages. It is available through Cohere's API and Microsoft Foundry.

models.name: IBM Granite 4.2 3B
models.context: 131,072 native (128K); IBM claims a 512K long-context extension
models.notable: The smallest member of the Apache 2.0 Granite 4.2 family, released alongside the 8B and 30B on Aug 25. Same dense decoder-only recipe as its siblings - grouped-query attention, RoPE, SwiGLU, RMSNorm, roughly 15 trillion pre-training tokens - with the switchable thinking mode that lets one checkpoint either reason step by step or answer directly. The key difference from the larger two: the 3B received foundational RL and alignment only and skipped the agentic reinforcement-learning stage, so IBM positions it for chat, summarization and on-device use rather than coding-agent work. Weights ship on Hugging Face, and it is the Granite 4.2 size targeted at Ollama and LM Studio on local hardware.

models.name: Ling-3.0-flash-Fin
models.params: 124B total, 5.1B active (mixture-of-experts; finance-tuned variant of Ling-3.0-flash)
models.notable: Ant Group's inclusionAI shipped a finance-domain build of Ling-3.0-flash, keeping the base model's 124B-total / 5.1B-active sparse mixture-of-experts architecture, its 262K-token context and 32K output limit, while post-training it for annual reports, financial workbooks and multi-document research. Ant pitches it at investment analysis, valuation modelling, information retrieval and banking workflows, and says it retains the base model's general reasoning, coding and math ability. Published agentic scores are 59.8 on Vals AI's Finance Agent v2, 29.2 on Mercor's APEX-Agents and 21.8 on SpreadsheetBench 2; trackers list it as not yet publicly ranked because coverage outside agentic evals is thin. Weights were announced for open release the following week, and Ant is running a one-month free API window through OpenRouter for finance professionals and developers.

models.name: Apodex 1.1
models.notable: Agentic reasoning model from a previously untracked lab, evaluated by Artificial Analysis on Aug 30 2026 at 44 on the Intelligence Index. Accompanying paper is titled 'Apodex 1.1: Scaling Agentic Intelligence for Complex Work' and frames the model around scaling executable training environments so agents can hold long-horizon work with state maintenance and recovery. 256K-token context, text and image input, text output, proprietary weights. Priced at $0.30 in / $3.00 out per 1M tokens with a 90% cache discount - cheap on input, expensive on output, which matters because the model is very verbose: it generated 180M output tokens across the Intelligence Index run versus a 67M median. A smaller Apodex-1.1-mini is published on Hugging Face.

models.name: Quasar 438B
models.notable: First frontier-scale model from Multiverse Computing, the San Sebastian quantum-inspired AI firm best known for CompactifAI, its tensor-network model-compression platform. Scored 43 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index when AA added it on Aug 31 2026. Text-only in and out, 1M-token context, proprietary weights, priced at $0.60 in / $1.80 out per 1M tokens - unusually cheap output for its tier. Arrives alongside the company's August 2026 Qualcomm partnership to put efficient models in data centers and a Series C targeting up to $570M.

models.name: Claude Fable 5.1
models.context: 1M (unchanged from Fable 5; not restated at launch)
models.modality: multimodal in, text out, adaptive reasoning with low/medium/high/xhigh/max effort
models.pricing: $10 in / $50 out per 1M; cache reads $0.25 per 1M (down 75% from Fable 5's $1.00)
models.notable: Anthropic's Sep 1 2026 refresh of the Mythos-class line and the new sole #1 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index: v4.1 scores it 66 at max effort, three points clear of Claude Opus 5 at 63, with 65 at xhigh, 62 at high, 60 at medium and 58 at low. Headline pricing is unchanged at $10/$50, but cache reads were cut 75% to $0.25 per 1M, which Anthropic says works out to roughly 25% cheaper for typical workloads and up to 45% for highly agentic ones. The gains are concentrated in long-horizon agentic coding and research: Terminal-Bench 4.0 rises to 55.8% from Fable 5's 42.0% (Opus 5 is 52.3%), Humanity's Last Exam reaches 60.9% without tools and 65.0% with, and AutomationBench nearly doubles to 31.4% from 17.1%. It also posts 52.6% on Terminal-Bench-Science, 73.4% on CursorBench 3.2.0, 77.9% partial / 41.7% strict on OSWorld 2.0 and 1853 Elo on GDPval-AA v2, above Opus 5's 1824. Anthropic says production safeguards now intervene about 60% less often, and shipped Enterprise Frontier Safeguards alongside it. Available as claude-fable-5-1 on the Anthropic API, AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure.

models.name: Claude Mythos 5.1
models.context: 1M (unchanged from Mythos 5; not restated at launch)
models.notable: The restricted-access sibling shipped the same day as Fable 5.1. The two share the same underlying model; Fable 5.1 is the generally available build carrying Anthropic's production safeguards, while Mythos 5.1 runs with those safeguards relaxed and is gated behind verification for cybersecurity and life-sciences organizations. That difference shows up directly on agentic coding: Mythos 5.1 scores 60.9% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 against Fable 5.1's 55.8%, a five-point gap attributable to safeguard routing rather than a different set of weights. Anthropic frames the 5.1 generation around long-running computer-programming work and scientific tasks such as experiment design, simulation and reading dense diagrams and tables.

models.name: Solaris
models.context: n/a - interactive session, not a token context window
models.modality: interactive interface generation (video-native); text prompt + mouse/keyboard input, rendered frames out
models.notable: Runway's first 'Interface World Model' - an AI system that generates a working application or website frame by frame as you interact with it, rather than emitting HTML, CSS, JavaScript or a component tree. It is built on Runway's Gen-4.5 video model, which already handles temporal coherence between frames; Solaris adds a feedback loop so the next frame is conditioned on user clicks and drags instead of a text trajectory, pairs the world model with a language model that reasons about intent, and distills multi-step diffusion down to a few steps for real-time response. Runway reports a user study of 250 participants across 30 examples (~7,500 pairwise judgments) in which people preferred Solaris to coded interfaces 61% of the time on instruction-following and 71% on natural in-scene behaviour. There are no independent benchmarks. Runway names text rendering, factual trustworthiness, coherence over long sessions and accessibility as open problems. Early access is by application only.

models.name: Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash
models.context: n/a - up to 10s of prior video as conditioning context; 40s cumulative output
models.modality: text-, image- and video-to-video generation with native audio; text and image in, video out
models.notable: Google's generative video model, moved to general availability on Aug 27 2026 as model ID gemini-omni-1.1-flash and pitched as the production-ready tier of the Omni line for media-editing and automated video workflows. The 1.1 update adds three things developers had been missing: scene extension in 10-second increments up to a 40-second cumulative clip (each extension conditioned on up to 10 seconds of prior context), explicit first-frame/last-frame control for clean transitions, and 4K upscaling on top of the existing 360p/720p/1080p tiers. A 360p draft tier generates up to 60% faster at roughly a third of the 720p cost, aimed at iteration before a full-quality render. Video reference conditioning is capped at three clips of up to three seconds each, and input videos must be 10 seconds or shorter unless extending the model's own output. Billing is token-based - $1.50 per 1M input, $9.00 per 1M text output and $17.50 per 1M video output tokens, with 720p video metering at 5,792 tokens per second, an effective ~$0.10 per second. It is live in Google AI Studio, the Gemini API and the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, in Google Flow and the Gemini app for AI Plus/Pro/Ultra subscribers, and already in production at Adobe Firefly, Figma Weave, GMI Cloud and Runway. Parameter count and architecture are undisclosed and there is no independent arena result.

models.name: Gemini 3.8 Flash
models.modality: multimodal in, text out, configurable reasoning effort (low/medium/high)
models.pricing: $0.75 in / $3.75 out per 1M (introductory rate through Dec 31 2026); rises to $1.50 / $7.50 on Jan 1 2027
models.notable: Google's fourth Flash model in under four months and its third budget-tier release in six weeks, shipped Sep 2 2026 while the frontier Gemini 3.5 Pro remains unreleased. It scores 59 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at high reasoning, up three points from Gemini 3.7 Flash's 56, which puts a $0.75/$3.75 model level with GPT-5.6 Sol at sub-maximum reasoning and Grok 4.6 at medium, and lands it on the intelligence-vs-cost-per-task Pareto frontier at $0.58 per task. The gains are concentrated in agentic work: DeepSWE v1.1 rises to 73.7% from 3.7 Flash's 65.3%, within striking distance of Claude Opus 5 at 74.0% and past GPT-5.6 Sol at 72.7%, while tau-3-Banking tool use jumps 12 points to 45%. It posts 54.9% on HLE-Verified. Google attributes the improvement to the model executing more reasoning steps and iteratively calling tools; Artificial Analysis measures roughly 30% more output tokens per task than 3.7 Flash and about 300 output tokens per second, with 2.5 minutes per task on high reasoning versus 0.8 minutes on low. Available via the Gemini API, Google AI Studio, Android Studio, Google Antigravity, Gemini Enterprise, and to AI Pro/Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app and Search.

models.name: Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber
models.modality: multimodal in, text out; cybersecurity-specialized agentic variant
models.pricing: not published; access-gated through the Fairwind Program
models.notable: The restricted sibling to Gemini 3.8 Flash, built to autonomously discover software vulnerabilities and write working patches, released the same day and available only to vetted defenders, government authorities and critical-infrastructure operators through Google's newly launched Fairwind Program. It reaches 86.2% on CyberGym, surpassing its predecessor 3.5 Flash Cyber and substantially larger frontier competitors, and Google reports an over-70% success rate on an internal vulnerability benchmark spanning twenty programming languages. On patching it posts 47.2% pass@1 on CWE-Bench. Google cites two external results: the Chrome Security team found it produced 2.6x more correct Chrome vulnerability patches than the best much-larger commercial models, and Wiz measured 7.5-9.7% higher recall on its internal penetration-testing benchmark at 2.3-5.2x lower cost than leading frontier models. Prompt-injection robustness also improved, with a 5.5% attack success rate on Gray Swan's indirect-prompt-injection suite. It lands one day after OpenAI disclosed that its unreleased Astra model is the first to cross 'Critical' on its cyber preparedness scale, making gated cyber-capable models the pattern across both labs.

models.name: Meta Muse Spark 1.3
models.modality: multimodal (text, image, video, document in; text out)
models.notable: Meta's third Muse Spark refresh in five weeks, shipped Sep 2 2026 into Muse Code and the Meta Model API as model ID muse-spark-1.3, and pitched by Mark Zuckerberg as frontier performance at low cost. Meta calls it its largest single jump in coding and agentic work to date: on its own published scorecard DeepSWE v1.1 rises to 75.4 from Muse Spark 1.2's 55.0 (Claude Opus 5 74.0), Terminal-Bench 2.1 reaches 88.8, tying GPT-5.6 Sol and ahead of Opus 5 at 86.7, and SWEAtlas CodeBase QnA hits 59.4 against Sol's 53.5 and Opus 5's 52.7. The clearest gap is long context: MRCR 256K-512K goes to 98.5 from 66.3 and MRCR 512K-1M to 98.1 from 55.5, versus 91.5 and 73.8 for GPT-5.6 Sol. On broad knowledge work it still trails Anthropic - GDPval-AA v2 1754 against Opus 5's 1824 - and OpenAI leads it on DeepSearch QA (93.0 vs 89.4) and the Agentic IF Index (60.5 vs 57.8). Meta reports roughly 20% fewer tool calls and 25% fewer tokens than 1.2 on internal coding comparisons, plus stronger adversarial robustness and more caution on irreversible actions. The 1M-token context and pricing are unchanged from 1.1 and 1.2 at $1.25 per 1M input, $0.15 cached and $4.25 output, with a contributor tier at $0.10/$0.20 in exchange for training rights. A max-reasoning mode is held back pending further safety testing, and Zuckerberg says open-weights versions are planned. Every number above is Meta's own, run on Meta's harness; Artificial Analysis has not yet published an independent Intelligence Index score, so 1.2's 57 remains Meta's last third-party mark.

models.name: Meta Muse Voice Transcribe
models.params: undisclosed (autoregressive multimodal model from the Muse Spark family)
models.context: streaming audio, processed in 80ms chunks; no fixed token context published
models.modality: audio in, streaming text out (real-time speech recognition with speaker diarization)
models.notable: Meta Superintelligence Labs' first real-time audio perception model, announced Sep 1 2026 and shipped the same day into the Meta AI Mac app, Muse Code and the Meta Model API. It is autoregressive rather than post-hoc: audio arrives in 80ms chunks, each converted to a soft token, and a reinforcement-learned 'adaptive delay' policy varies how long the model waits per word based on difficulty, so easy words emit immediately while ambiguous ones buy extra context. Meta reports a 3.1% word error rate on Artificial Analysis's streaming speech-to-text benchmark, which it claims is first place, a 17.5% diarization error rate across standard datasets, and a final transcript roughly 0.16 seconds after a speaker stops. It handles 20-plus simultaneous speakers, was trained across 70-plus languages with 25 extensively validated (including Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam), and follows code-switching within a single sentence. Meta says audio is processed but not stored.
